content: Certainly. Ethinylestradiol can increase the levels or effects of tazemetostat by influencing the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Conversely, tazemetostat can decrease the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate through the same enzymatic pathway. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Tecovirimat, a weak inducer of CYP3A4, can reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be closely monitored for effectiveness when co-administered. Teriflunomide increases the levels of ethinylestradiol through an unknown mechanism. Close monitoring is recommended. Tetracycline can decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Alternative methods of contraception may be considered in serious cases. Ferrous fumarate reduces the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Close monitoring is advised. Ethinylestradiol can increase the levels or effects of theophylline by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of thyroid desiccated by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Tigecycline reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Tipranavir can significantly alter estrogen plasma levels, either increasing or decreasing them, which may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of tizanidine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects of tizanidine, such as hypotension or bradycardia. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of tolterodine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. In serious cases, alternative drugs should be considered. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable during co-administration. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Tovorafenib, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with hormonal contraceptives. If unavoidable, use an additional effective non-hormonal contraceptive method during co-administration and for 28 days after discontinuation. Tranexamic acid and ethinylestradiol increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of thrombosis. Co-administration is contraindicated. Ethinylestradiol may decrease the oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), potentially increasing serum concentrations and adverse effects. Close monitoring is recommended. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting its metabolism. This may increase serum concentrations of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Ferrous fumarate and trientine reduce each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. Trimethoprim reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A substrates according to product labeling and monitor closely. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of ursodiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Vadadustat increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and may increase the exposure of BCRP substrates. Ferrous fumarate reduces the levels or effects of vadadustat by drug binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer vadadustat at least 1 hour before oral iron supplements or iron-containing products. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Ethinylestradiol and valoctocogene roxaparvovec may increase the risk of hepatotoxicity when combined. Monitor liver enzymes closely and consider alternative medications if potential drug interactions arise. Ethinylestradiol decreases the levels or effects of valproic acid by increasing its elimination, which may lead to increased seizure frequency. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Vitamin E reduces the levels of ferrous fumarate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Monitor closely. Vonoprazan reduces the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended.
